raw_text:
# 12-Week Post-Cardiac Rehab Fitness Programme

**Client profile:** 58-year-old male, 6 months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise only.

## Key Safety Parameters
- **HR cap:** 115 bpm (70% age-predicted max). Use a chest-strap HR monitor every session. Pause/reduce intensity if exceeded.
- **RPE target:** 11–13 on Borg 6–20 scale (light to somewhat hard); never above 14.
- **No Valsalva:** Coach continuous exhalation through the concentric (lifting) phase. No breath-holding. Avoid overhead pressing with heavy load early on, avoid isometric holds >10 sec, avoid inversions.
- **No max lifts:** Always leave 3–5 reps in reserve (RIR). Hard cap at RPE 7/10.
- **Warm-up:** 8–10 min low-intensity cycling or walking, HR gradually rising to ~90–100 bpm before resistance work.
- **Cool-down:** 5–10 min walking + mobility, HR returned <100 bpm before leaving.
- **Red flags:** Stop session for chest pain/pressure, unusual dyspnoea, dizziness, palpitations, claudication. Have him carry GTN spray if prescribed.
- **Frequency:** 3 sessions/week (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri) with active recovery walks on off-days.

---

## PHASE 1 — Foundation & Reconditioning (Weeks 1–4)

**Goals:** Establish movement competency, build aerobic base, habituate to resistance training, monitor HR/BP response.

**Session structure:** ~50–55 min total
- Warm-up 10 min (recumbent bike, RPE 10–11)
- Resistance circuit (machines, full body)
- Steady-state cardio 15 min
- Cool-down + mobility 10 min

**Resistance prescription:** 2 sets × 12–15 reps, RPE 11–12, ~60–90 sec rest. Machines preferred (supported, controlled ROM, easy to grade load).

### Week 1
**Session A & B & C (same template, alternate days):**
1. Seated leg press — 2×12
2. Seated chest press (machine) — 2×12
3. Seated row (machine) — 2×12
4. Lat pulldown — 2×12
5. Seated leg curl — 2×12
6. Standing calf raise — 2×15
7. Dead bug — 2×8/side
8. Cardio: recumbent bike, 15 min, HR 95–110

### Week 2
Same exercises. Progress load only if RPE ≤11 and HR stable.
- Add 1 set to leg press and chest press (now 3×12)
- Cardio: 17 min, HR 100–112

### Week 3
Introduce light free-weight patterns:
1. Goblet squat (box target) — 2×10, light DB
2. Chest press machine — 3×12
3. DB Romanian deadlift (light, hip hinge focus) — 2×10
4. Seated cable row — 3×12
5. Lat pulldown — 2×12
6. Seated DB shoulder press (light, neutral grip, never overhead lockout under strain) — 2×10
7. Pallof press — 2×10/side
8. Cardio: bike or treadmill walk (incline), 18 min

### Week 4 (Deload-light, assessment)
- All resistance: 2×12 at week 3 loads (no progression)
- Cardio: 20 min steady, HR 100–112
- Reassess: resting HR, RPE responses, BP pre/post, 6-min walk test if feasible

---

## PHASE 2 — Progressive Loading (Weeks 5–8)

**Goals:** Increase resistance volume, introduce more compound free-weight work, add interval-style cardio (still sub-threshold), develop work capacity.

**Session split:** A/B alternating
- Day A: Lower-body emphasis + cardio
- Day B: Upper-body emphasis + cardio
- Day C: Full-body circuit + longer steady cardio

**Resistance prescription:** 2–3 sets × 10–12 reps, RPE 12–13, 90 sec rest.

### Session A — Lower body
1. Goblet squat — 3×10
2. DB Romanian deadlift — 3×10
3. Leg press — 2×12
4. Seated leg curl — 2×12
5. Standing calf raise — 2×15
6. Side plank (knees) — 2×20 sec/side
7. Cardio: bike intervals — 2 min @ RPE 12 / 2 min @ RPE 10, ×5 (20 min), HR cap 113

### Session B — Upper body
1. DB bench press (flat, light–moderate) — 3×10
2. Chest-supported DB row — 3×10
3. Lat pulldown — 2×12
4. Seated cable row, neutral grip — 2×12
5. DB lateral raise — 2×12
6. Cable triceps pushdown — 2×12
7. DB hammer curl — 2×12
8. Pallof press — 2×10/side
9. Cardio: treadmill incline walk, 20 min, HR 100–113

### Session C — Full body
1. Leg press — 2×12
2. Chest press machine — 2×12
3. Seated row — 2×12
4. DB step-up (low box, light) — 2×8/leg
5. Bird dog — 2×8/side
6. Cardio: 25 min steady, bike or walk, RPE 11–12

### Weekly progression W5 → W8
- W5: introduce template at conservative loads
- W6: +5–10% load on machines if RPE ≤12; cardio intervals add one round
- W7: +1 set to two main lifts per session
- W8: hold loads, focus on tempo (3-sec eccentric); extend steady cardio to 25–28 min

---

## PHASE 3 — Consolidation & Capacity (Weeks 9–12)

**Goals:** Build durable strength endurance, raise sustainable aerobic workload, integrate functional patterns relevant to daily life, prepare him for a sustainable long-term routine.

**Resistance prescription:** 3 sets × 8–12 reps, RPE 12–13, 90–120 sec rest. Still no Valsalva, still 3–5 RIR.

### Session A — Lower body + carry
1. Goblet squat — 3×10
2. DB Romanian deadlift — 3×8
3. DB reverse lunge (supported, light) — 2×8/leg
4. Leg curl — 2×12
5. Calf raise — 2×15
6. Suitcase carry (moderate DB, 20 m, breathing freely) — 2 rounds/side
7. Cardio: bike intervals — 3 min @ RPE 13 / 2 min @ RPE 10, ×4 (20 min), HR cap 115

### Session B — Upper body
1. DB bench press — 3×8
2. One-arm DB row (bench-supported) — 3×8/side
3. Lat pulldown — 3×10
4. Cable chest fly — 2×12
5. Seated DB shoulder press, neutral grip — 2×10
6. Face pull — 2×12
7. Biceps & triceps superset — 2×12 each
8. Cardio: incline treadmill walk, 25 min, HR 105–115

### Session C — Conditioning & function
1. Sled push (light, walking pace — emphasise breathing) — 4×20 m
2. Goblet squat — 2×10
3. Chest-supported row — 2×12
4. Farmer's carry — 3×30 m
5. Dead bug + Pallof press circuit — 2 rounds
6. Cardio finisher: 20 min steady at top of zone (HR 110–115), RPE 13

### Weekly progression W9 → W12
- W9: introduce template, conservative loads
- W10: +5% load main lifts if all RPE/HR markers in range
- W11: extend conditioning interval blocks by 1 round; carries +10 m
- W12: **Reassessment week** — repeat baseline tests (6-min walk, resting/recovery HR, BP, subjective wellbeing, lift loads). Plan next 12-week block based on data.

---

## Active Recovery (Off-days)

- 2–3× per week: 20–40 min brisk walking outdoors, RPE 10–11, HR <110
- Daily mobility: 5–10 min thoracic, hip, ankle work
- Sleep: aim 7–8 hr; flag any new orthopnoea/PND to GP immediately

---

## Monitoring Log (every session)

Record: resting HR, peak HR, BP pre/post (if you have a cuff), RPE per block, any symptoms, loads lifted. Review monthly with his GP or cardiac rehab team.

## Communication Points

- Encourage him to keep his cardiologist and GP informed of programme progression.
- If he's on **beta-blockers**, HR will be blunted — lean more heavily on RPE (cap 13) than HR numbers, and discuss appropriate target HR with his cardiologist as the 70% rule may not apply cleanly.
- Hydration before/during sessions; avoid training in the 60–90 min after a heavy meal.

This programme is intentionally conservative — the priority across all 12 weeks is consistency, symptom-free training, and building his confidence in exercise as a long-term part of cardiac risk reduction.
